_comment: Octail's own egg (no upstream file), with the Terraria variables of terraria-vanilla.json. TShock for Linux x64 from Pryaxis' GitHub releases (latest or a tag), checked against GitHub's SHA-256 digest of the asset or a pinned SHA-256 (no checksum: the install fails), failures exit non-zero. TShock 6 is framework-dependent .NET 9, so it runs on dotnet_9 (dotnet_10 with DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major as the alternative). serverconfig.txt gets the world, port, players, MOTD, seed, password and NPC stream before every start (properties parser, as the vanilla egg); the port, player cap and REST API are also set on TShock's command line, which overrides tshock/config.json. Octail turns the REST API on by default (REST_API, on its own allocated port, REST_PORT) so the Players tab works without extra setup; the owner can switch it off. The Players tab (tshock preset) lists over the REST API with no auth at all (confirmed on a live server) and kicks, bans and broadcasts with a session token Tentacle fetches itself at runtime (GET /v2/token/create) using a seeded account: TShock ships with zero accounts until a real game client runs /setup <code> in chat, which an unattended install can't do, and the obvious-looking fix (a bare token in config.json's ApplicationRestTokens) crashes TShock's config load or (as an object) issues a token that doesn't work, confirmed by hand against a live TShock 6.2.1 server. The install script instead inserts a superadmin row straight into tshock/tshock.sqlite before the first start, with TSHOCK_API_PASSWORD (generated by Octail, same as other eggs' generated RCON/admin passwords) bcrypt-hashed by htpasswd; the account is named octail-tentacle and is for Tentacle's own use only, never shown or logged in with from the panel. Generic TCP idle sleep (off until staff enable it per server), say as the broadcast, off saves and stops.
name: Terraria TShock
author: eggs@octail.net
description: TShock, the Terraria server mod for communities: permissions and groups, anti-cheat, server-side characters, bans, region protection and plugins.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# TShock (Octail's own install script): the TShock release for Linux x64 from Pryaxis' GitHub releases (latest or a
# tag), checked against the SHA-256 digest GitHub lists for the asset or a pinned SHA-256, failures exit non-zero.
# Worlds (saves/), TShock's database and config (tshock/) and plugins added by the owner stay on reinstall;
# serverconfig.txt is only written when there is none.
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
set -euo pipefail
# Downloads are staged on the server disk: the install container's /tmp is a small tmpfs.
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.octail-install
trap 'rm -rf /mnt/server/.octail-install' EXIT
apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y -qq curl jq unzip tar ca-certificates sqlite3 apache2-utils > /dev/null

VERSION="${TSHOCK_VERSION:-latest}"
if [ "$VERSION" = "latest" ]; then
    API="https://api.github.com/repos/Pryaxis/TShock/releases/latest"
else
    API="https://api.github.com/repos/Pryaxis/TShock/releases/tags/v${VERSION#v}"
fi
if ! RELEASE=$(curl -fsSL "$API"); then
    echo "Installation failed: TShock release ${VERSION} wasn't found on GitHub."
    exit 1
fi
TAG=$(echo "$RELEASE" | jq -r '.tag_name')
ASSET=$(echo "$RELEASE" | jq -r '[.assets[] | select(.name | test("linux-x64-Release\\.zip$"))][0] // empty')
if [ -z "$ASSET" ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: release ${TAG} has no Linux x64 build."
    exit 1
fi
NAME=$(echo "$ASSET" | jq -r '.name')
URL=$(echo "$ASSET" | jq -r '.browser_download_url')
DIGEST=$(echo "$ASSET" | jq -r '.digest // empty')
SUM="${TSHOCK_SHA256:-}"
if [ -z "$SUM" ]; then
    SUM="${DIGEST#sha256:}"
fi
if [ -z "$SUM" ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: GitHub lists no checksum for ${NAME}; set TShock SHA-256 to the file's checksum."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Downloading ${NAME} (${TAG})"
curl -fsSL -o /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock.zip "$URL"
if ! echo "${SUM,,}  /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock.zip" | sha256sum -c --quiet -; then
    rm -f /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock.zip
    echo "Installation failed: the download doesn't match its SHA-256."
    exit 1
fi
rm -rf /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock /mnt/server
unzip -q -o /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock.zip -d /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock </dev/null
# The zip holds one tar that keeps the file modes (TShock.Server is executable).
for archive in /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock/*.tar; do
    if [ -f "$archive" ]; then
        tar -xf "$archive" -C /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock
        rm -f "$archive"
    fi
done
if [ ! -f /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock/TShock.Server ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: ${NAME} has no TShock.Server."
    exit 1
fi
cp -a /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock/. /mnt/server/
rm -rf /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock /mnt/server/.octail-install/tshock.zip

cd /mnt/server
chmod +x TShock.Server
mkdir -p saves/Worlds tshock ServerPlugins
if [ ! -f serverconfig.txt ]; then
    cat > serverconfig.txt <<'OCTAIL_EOF'
worldpath=/home/container/saves/Worlds
worldname=world
world=/home/container/saves/Worlds/world.wld
difficulty=0
autocreate=1
maxplayers=8
OCTAIL_EOF
fi

if [ ! -x /mnt/server/TShock.Server ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: TShock.Server is missing."
    exit 1
fi

# Octail: seed a superadmin account in TShock's own database for Tentacle's REST calls (Players tab).
# TShock ships with zero accounts until a real game client runs /setup <code> in chat, which an
# unattended install can't do. config.json's ApplicationRestTokens field looks like a way around this
# but isn't: a bare token there crashes the config load, and a {"Username": ...} value there parses but
# every request then fails with "the provided token became invalid due to group changes" (no real
# account backs it). Writing the account straight into tshock.sqlite before first start works instead:
# TShock's bcrypt check accepts a hash from htpasswd, and Tentacle fetches a session token itself at
# runtime with this username/password (tentacle/src/players/index.js, GET /v2/token/create).
if [ -z "${TSHOCK_API_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: no Tentacle account password was generated for this server."
    exit 1
fi
sqlite3 tshock/tshock.sqlite "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Users (ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, Username TEXT UNIQUE, Password TEXT, UUID TEXT, Usergroup TEXT, Registered TEXT, LastAccessed TEXT, KnownIPs TEXT);"
TENTACLE_SEEDED=$(sqlite3 tshock/tshock.sqlite "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Users WHERE Username='octail-tentacle';")
if [ "$TENTACLE_SEEDED" = "0" ]; then
    TENTACLE_HASH=$(htpasswd -bnBC 10 "" "$TSHOCK_API_PASSWORD" | cut -d: -f2)
    sqlite3 tshock/tshock.sqlite "INSERT INTO Users (Username, Password, UUID, Usergroup, Registered) VALUES ('octail-tentacle', '${TENTACLE_HASH}', '', 'superadmin', datetime('now'));"
fi

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed: TShock ${TAG}."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: TShock version
variables.description: latest or a release such as 6.2.1 (each TShock release supports one Terraria version; players need that one). Reinstall to switch.

variables.name: TShock SHA-256
variables.description: Optional: the SHA-256 of the release's Linux x64 zip, to pin the download. Empty: the checksum GitHub lists for it.

variables.name: World name
variables.description: The name for the world file.

variables.name: Max players
variables.description: The maximum number of players a server will hold (1-255).

variables.name: World size
variables.description: The size of a new world: 1 (small), 2 (medium), 3 (large).

variables.name: Difficulty
variables.description: The difficulty of a new world: 0 (classic), 1 (expert), 2 (master), 3 (journey).

variables.name: World seed
variables.description: The seed for a new world. Empty: random.

variables.name: Password
variables.description: The server password. Empty: none (TShock accounts still apply).

variables.name: NPC stream
variables.description: Reduces enemy skipping but uses more bandwidth. The lower the number the less skipping, 0 is off.

variables.name: REST API
variables.description: true turns on TShock's REST API on the REST port, which the Players tab uses to list, kick, ban and message everyone; false keeps it off (the Players tab then shows nobody).

variables.name: REST port
variables.description: The REST API port, an allocation of its own (set when the server is created).

variables.name: Tentacle account password
variables.description: Generated by Octail when the server is created; bcrypt-hashed into a seeded TShock account (octail-tentacle) the install script creates so Tentacle can use the REST API for the Players tab. Internal only: never used to log into the game.
